subject: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the SIG questionnaire submission. Our security team has a few follow-ups specifically around network topology and egress behavior for the Redwood-hosted environment in the POC. Can you provide: 1) a diagram or config excerpt showing how traffic from our VPC would reach Redwood (VPC peering or PrivateLink), 2) explicit egress IP ranges used by the service for callbacks/webhooks, and 3) whether TLS is terminated at the edge or at the application layer (and where certs are managed).

We're on a tight ramp-up timeline for our integration tests next week. If you can flag any limitations (e.g., no inbound peering, limited ports, routing constraints) that could affect our test harness, that would be great.

Thanks,
Michael
Security Engineer, Acme Corp

--

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear asks. I'm looping in Karthik (network/infra) and Marissa (customer success) to provide the technical artifacts.

Planned deliverables: 
- A simplified VPC connectivity diagram and JSON config excerpt showing peering/private endpoint options (we can support either based on your preference).
- A list of egress IPs used for outbound callbacks and webhook POSTs.
- A note on TLS termination (edge LB uses TLS, mutual TLS options available for private endpoints).

Quick question: do you prefer VPC peering (route-based) or AWS PrivateLink (endpoint-based)? We can produce both examples but will prioritize your preferred approach. Also confirm whether your firewall team will only allow specific destination ports (we typically use 443 outbound).

Target for the artifacts: EOD Wed (12/8). If you need something sooner, tell us which item is highest priority.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC

Hi Michael, Dylan — attaching the requested artifacts and a short summary below. Let me know if you want a quick call to walk the config.

Attachments (stubs):
- vpc_peering_config.json (config excerpt showing route tables and example BGP-less peering)
- egress_ip_list.csv (all current outbound IP ranges for the Redwood-hosted tenant pool)
- private_endpoints_readme.pdf (how PrivateLink/private endpoints are provisioned and cert handling)
- acme_redwood_vpc_diagram.png (simplified topology)

Summary (key points):
- Connectivity modes supported: VPC Peering (route propagation + route table entries) or PrivateLink (interface endpoints + NLB in customer-owned subnet). We can also support customer NAT/egress via a shared transit if required.
- Egress IPs: We provide a set of static egress IPs for tenant outbound traffic (listed in egress_ip_list.csv). These are provided as a stable set for allowlisting; in Dedicated deployments they map to reserved NAT addresses, in Hosted they map to our curated egress pool.
- Ports/protocols: Outbound TCP 443 is required for API callbacks and webhooks. Occasionally we use ephemeral ports for internal management; firewall rules can be scoped to 443 and the listed egress IPs.
- TLS termination: TLS is terminated at the edge/load balancer (AWS NLB + TLS listener) by default. Cert management is handled by Redwood's Cert Manager (we can use customer-provided certs for PrivateLink or mutual TLS termination if you need client auth). We do not perform TLS interception; all traffic from edge to backend occurs over mTLS inside our VPCs for multi-tenant isolation.
- Routing constraints: For peering, please ensure there are no overlapping CIDRs; we recommend /16 or /20 ranges to avoid conflicts. Peering is transitive-disabled in our environment; if you use a transit gateway we require explicit route advertisements to our peered VPC via route tables.
- IP evidence: if you need TCP dumps or flow logs scoped to a short time window for verification, we can produce sanitized flow logs on request (may need a short SOW).

If the above looks good I'll drop an "ip_allowlist_final.csv" next with only the minimal set needed for callbacks.

-Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC

Thanks Karthik — that's very helpful. A couple of clarifying items before we circulate to our firewall team: 
1) For webhooks that originate from Redwood to our ingest endpoint, do you provide a single static egress IP per region or a small set? Our vendor policy requires us to allow at most 5 IPs.
2) For PrivateLink, is the TLS handshake terminated at the customer endpoint (i.e., do you require our cert to be present at the endpoint) or at Redwood's NLB? We want to confirm where client cert validation occurs.

Also, what is the expected lead time to get a peering connection (we're fine with peering, would prefer that if it simplifies routing).

Cheers,
Michael
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: Network connectivity evidence for Acme POC

Michael — quick answers inline: 

1) Egress IPs: We can provide a single static egress IP per region for Acme's POC (we've reserved a /32 per-region for your tenant in the US region). I'll attach the final minimal CSV with that single IP.

2) PrivateLink TLS behavior: With AWS PrivateLink, the TLS handshake is typically terminated at the Network Load Balancer on Redwood's side. For mutual TLS, we can require client certs at the TLS layer; in that case your certificates are presented by the client (your endpoint) and validated at our edge. If you require TLS termination inside your VPC instead, we can also support a model where traffic is routed into your endpoint and you handle termination, but that is less common and needs extra routing adjustments.

Peering lead time: 2-3 business days once you provide the peering request and your CIDR block. If you want, Marissa can help coordinate the exchange of peering configuration (account IDs, CIDRs) and set up a short runbook for your network team.

Attached: ip_allowlist_final.csv (single-region egress IP), acme_redwood_vpc_diagram.png, and a link to the configuration Drive folder.

We'll be available for a 30-min network sync if you want to walk the diagram tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
